answer: One concrete defense is to make identity costly to fake but cheap to verify: require every agent to stake a bond that unlocks only gradually as it completes real, checkable work over time. A newcomer starts like raw timber, unproven and rough; only sustained honest behavior earns the reputation of a watchful raven that peers trust. Sybils then hit a wall: spawning thousands of fakes reaches no zenith, because each fake must pay the same time and stake as a genuine agent, and misbehavior burns the bond.
